nodes.rationale: The free Supabase tier has no automatic backups, and pet cards plus the Telegram-to-Altegio link exist nowhere else (Altegio has no animal records at all). The dump goes to Telegram rather than the PythonAnywhere disk: a copy on the same machine as the bot does not survive account problems, i.e. it fails to cover half the scenarios a backup exists for. api.telegram.org is already whitelisted on the proxy, Telegram keeps file history, so it costs nothing and adds no infrastructure. Format is one readable JSON file (jsonb and array columns would be flattened irreversibly by CSV), no gzip while the file stays in kilobytes.

nodes.label: Keyset Pagination of Table Reads
nodes.rationale: Reading by offset (.range()) defines the next window by how much was already read, so a row deleted between two requests (delete_pet, delete_pending_notifications_for_record from the Altegio webhook are real runtime deletions) shifts everything after it and one row silently misses the dump. Reading from the last key is immune, which is why the sort column must be unique and NOT NULL — nullable would give .gt(col, None) and an infinite loop. The loop exits on an empty page, not a short one: PAGE_SIZE is only our assumption about the PostgREST ceiling, and a smaller server-side db-max-rows would make 'short page' a false end-of-table signal, at the cost of one extra empty request per table.

nodes.label: Explicit BACKUP_TABLES Registry
nodes.rationale: Supabase REST cannot enumerate tables, so the list is a constant — with the useful side effect that adding a table forces a conscious decision about the backup, hence the post-migration checklist entry. It is a mapping table -> sort column rather than a plain list because there is no shared sort column: seven tables key on id, cron_state on the textual key. cron_state is included despite being operational state: four rows cost nothing and exclusion logic would be extra code.

nodes.label: Weekly Cadence Gating via cron_state
nodes.rationale: The weekly mark is the date of this week's Saturday rather than an ISO week number, because cron_state.last_run_date is a date column; Saturday and Sunday resolve to the same mark, so the Sunday catch-up (for when the external cron sleeps through Saturday) cannot fire twice. Hour 7 avoids 9 and 10 when other tasks message clients. The decision lives in the pure function is_backup_due(now, last_run, last_attempt) so the cadence is testable without mocking the scheduler; the dispatcher only writes marks. The success mark is written only after confirmed delivery.

nodes.label: Separate BACKUP_CHAT_ID Recipient
nodes.rationale: The dump carries client names and phone numbers, so it goes to the owner's private chat and must have no chance of landing in the shared staff group; the value lives only in .env and PythonAnywhere env vars, never as a default in config.py. Because the admin group is configured by a different variable, that channel is alive exactly when BACKUP_CHAT_ID is missing — which is the most likely production failure, so an unset variable notifies admins instead of only writing a log line nobody reads.

nodes.label: Loud Failure Principle
nodes.rationale: A backup that quietly stops working for half a year is worse than no backup — at least a missing one is known. Hence: any Supabase or Telegram failure logs and notifies the admin topic, the success mark is never written on failure, and the caption lists every table's row count including zeros (a review round removed the 'if n' filter, because a table that suddenly arrives empty from revoked rights or a rename would otherwise just vanish from the only artefact the owner actually reads).

nodes.label: Deliberately No Restore Script
nodes.rationale: It could only be verified against the live database (risking real data) or a separate test Supabase project, and an unverified restore script gives a false sense of safety. The full dump stays, and restore is written at the moment of need. Revisit if a test project appears. Encryption is also skipped: a password stored in the same private chat adds nothing.

nodes.label: Spec: AI Grounded Context and Injection Defence
nodes.norm_label: spec: ai grounded context and injection defence

nodes.label: Prompt Injection Defence by Construction
nodes.rationale: Client-written questionnaire fields (pet name, breed string, allergies, behaviour notes) are stored forever and could contain 'ignore previous instructions'. Instead of filtering them, the breed is used only as a Python-side lookup key into the Altegio catalog; the model only ever sees admin-written service titles (which already encode the breed) and numeric weight. The injection surface disappears by construction rather than by filter, at the accepted UX cost that the bot says 'for your Yorkie' instead of 'for Barney'.

nodes.label: Deterministic Amount Validation of Model Output
nodes.rationale: Prompt rules are bypassable and are explicitly not a security boundary; the boundary is this post-check. Every hryvnia amount in the reply is regex-extracted, normalised (spaces, NBSP, commas, prefix/suffix currency, UAH) and compared numerically against AiContext.amounts, which contains every number that actually went into the context block including the range bounds. A single unknown amount replaces the whole reply with a deterministic price list. It is a post-check: Groq has already been called, only the display is suppressed. Known limit: amounts written as words are not caught, judged disproportionate to parse.
nodes.norm_label: deterministic amount validation of model output

nodes.label: Ban on Price Totals
nodes.rationale: A sum of two real prices is not in the context, so the strict check would reject it anyway. Forbidding totals in the prompt was chosen over widening the check to pairwise sums (18 positions = 153 combinations), because widening weakens the single real guard. Non-technical reason too: the final amount is confirmed by the groomer on inspection, so a bot confidently saying 'together 1500' promises what it does not control.

nodes.label: Outbound Link Whitelist
nodes.rationale: The model has no internet, but data-borne text could still coax it into printing a foreign URL. Only the booking widget URL survives. Review round hardened this: host comparison via urllib.parse instead of startswith (so '?u=https://evil.com' and glued URLs no longer pass), plus a ban on a second scheme in the remainder, and whitespace is only renormalised when something was actually cut so newlines in ordinary replies survive.

nodes.label: Per-User AI Rate Limit
nodes.rationale: 15 messages per hour per tg_user_id on a sliding in-memory window. Protects the shared free Groq quota from a single user hammering the chat; on exceeding it Groq is not called at all (the only path where the model is skipped) and the client gets the same deterministic salon-phone text used for exhausted quota, so no third fallback wording is introduced.

nodes.label: Groq Quota Digest at 18:30
nodes.rationale: A daily gate fired at the first 429 would list exactly one affected client and never mention anyone hit later that day, so 'list for the day' would in practice mean 'first victim'. A fixed-time digest lets the set accumulate. 18:30 sits right after the 18:00 booking-incomplete notice so admins process both lists at once in working hours; the minute component forces now.time() comparison instead of the project's usual now.hour. Sent through the synchronous notify_admins because the cron path deliberately bypasses the event loop. Accepted limits: the owner learns at 18:30 rather than immediately, and a process restart loses the in-memory set.

nodes.label: In-Process Catalog Cache with Stale Fallback
nodes.rationale: Catalog TTL one hour, branch directory one day, kept in process memory on purpose: the alternative (a daily Supabase snapshot) means a new table, a new migration, a new BACKUP_TABLES row and up-to-a-day staleness for data that changes a few times a year. On Altegio failure the expired entry is served anyway with a WARNING — an old price list beats no prices, accepted at the cost that withdrawn services can be quoted for a long time with no signal other than the log line.
nodes.norm_label: in-process catalog cache with stale fallback

nodes.label: Client Isolation by Telegram User ID
nodes.rationale: Context is built solely from the tg_user_id supplied by Telegram; no client identifier is ever accepted from message text, so one client's data cannot surface in another's conversation.
nodes.norm_label: client isolation by telegram user id

nodes.label: Sanitisation of the Trusted Source
nodes.rationale: Service titles and addresses are written by salon admins in Altegio — not hostile input, but not sterile either. Each value is flattened, truncated to 120 chars and stripped of the '===' sequence that delimits the data block, so a title cannot close the block and start issuing instructions. A review round rejected an interim blacklist of phrases ('КІНЕЦЬ ДАНИХ', 'ДАНІ САЛОНУ') as unscalable: removing '===' alone already makes a full boundary marker unforgeable.

nodes.label: Graceful Degradation of Context Assembly
nodes.rationale: Context assembly may never break the chat, because AI is the fallback for everything the client types. Altegio down with cache -> stale cache; without cache -> context with no prices; Supabase down -> client treated as unregistered; any other error -> base prompt with no context; Groq 429 -> phone text plus digest; other Groq error -> apology.

nodes.label: Guard Trip Visibility Counter
nodes.rationale: Catches the scenario where Groq swaps the model or the prompt drifts and the bot silently enters permanent-fallback mode: such a break produces a steady stream of rejections, so five in an hour raises one admin alert, at most hourly. Same principle as the backup module — a silent failure is worse than a loud one. Review corrected the docstring claim that the counter survives a restart: in-memory state does not, the threshold simply refills.

nodes.label: Chat History Trimming
nodes.rationale: History previously grew until process restart, dragging tokens and latency; trimmed to the last 10 messages (about five exchanges). A fix round added that the window must not start with a leading assistant message, otherwise the model receives an answer to a question it cannot see. On any Groq error the unanswered user message is popped so the user/assistant pairing stays consistent.

nodes.label: backup_attempt Mark: Two Attempts per Week
nodes.source_location: ### 1. Стійкий збій ретраївся на кожному тику
nodes.rationale: Gating on the success mark alone meant a persistent failure retried on every cron tick: the external cron knocks every ~10 minutes, so from Saturday 07:00 to end of Sunday the branch would run about 246 times — 246 full dumps of eight Supabase reads each and 246 admin-topic messages. A second cron_state mark keyed on the attempt, at day granularity and written before the run, reduces this to the intended two attempts per week while keeping the Sunday catch-up. The third parameter of is_backup_due is deliberately required with no default so a caller cannot silently forget it, and no date comparison leaked into the dispatcher. No migration needed: cron_state is key/value with upsert on conflict.
